title: Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits of coherent formal modules
statement: Let X be Noetherian, I a quasi-coherent ideal and U an open subscheme with its Noetherian instance. The explicit full-subcategory termwise restriction functor defined by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-restriction-objects] preserves finite limits and finite colimits in Coh(X,I) and Coh(U,I|U), whose abelianness is [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. This is a preservation statement only; it asserts no local reflection of exactness.

proof.text: Cokernels are termwise by the abelian theorem, and ordinary module restriction preserves them as a left adjoint.

proof.text: For the stabilized kernel construction, restrict sectionwise kernels, locally defined images and ideal products. Restriction preserves the cokernel quotients. A global stabilization bound works locally; a common larger bound identifies constructions using different bounds, including their maps into the source. The restricted fork is therefore a kernel fork.

proof.text: Finite biproduct identities restrict termwise. In abelian categories finite products together with kernels give finite limits; finite coproducts together with cokernels give finite colimits. Apply these criteria to the explicit additive lift.

    [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.Opens)

    PreservesFiniteLimits (coherentFormalModulesRestriction I U) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (coherentFormalModulesRestriction I U)
